gate_claims.claim: the card also lists regression.run, which is not available here (the tool is CONTRACT_ONLY)
the card lists test.run and regression.run and the phrases 'Over-constrained stimulus' and 'Stimulus reaches coverage goals' (the document says 'reaches coverage goals')
the test tool this skill holds (test.run) is available
the simulation gate passes only its own nonce argument to the run: Icarus gets '+nirmaan_nonce=<nonce>' and nothing else (so a seed has to live in the testbench source)
the same for the Verilator simulation: the built binary gets only the nonce argument
the Verilator simulation builds with 'verilator --binary' and the sources alone, no hand-written C++ file (supports the inference that no C++ harness is needed)
the testbench is the file that declares the run's top module
only the testbench may call $finish, $stop, $exit, read plusargs ($value$plusargs, $test$plusargs), open files, or use $system, $c or DPI; the list is TESTBENCH_ONLY

a design file using any of them is refused before anything runs (the file declaring the top is skipped, every other file is scanned, and the refusal says 'nothing was simulated'; run locally with $finish in a design file)
the same refusal is the check of both simulators for both simulation tools
a design file that reads the nonce plusarg is refused (test: spy design with $value$plusargs, both simulators)
the verdict line is 'NIRMAAN-SIM <nonce> <passed> passed, <failed> failed': the nonce, a count passed and a count failed
a verdict with another nonce is not counted as the run's verdict and fails the run
the run fails when the verdict is missing, repeated, reports a failed check, or reports no passed check
the five verdict failures (no verdict, another nonce, no check passed, a failed check, two verdicts) each fail the run (test)
the gate by itself asks only for at least one passed check; a run of ten passed checks passes with no bound (run locally: parse_simulation of a verdict '10 passed, 0 failed' passed with checks 10)
the simulation result reports a 'checks' count (and checks_failed)
the backend hands the parser's metrics, including checks, to the tool outcome
a bound is a metric, a direction (max or min) and a value
a bound is written metric>=value, so 'checks>=N' parses to metric checks, op min, value N (run locally: Bound.parse('checks>=100'))
a workflow requirement can carry bounds, and a run counts only if checked against each
the CLI takes a bound as --bound

a passing run that breaks a bound, or never reported the metric, is failed (run locally: checks>=100 with 10 checks failed 'checks 10 is below min_checks 100'; with 100 checks passed; with checks not reported failed 'checks was not reported')
a requirement counts only runs checked against its bounds (test)

no requirement in the shipped workflows sets a bound on a simulation run's checks: every bounds= use in the shipped workflows names latches, proven, test_coverage, text_bytes, drc_violations, unconnected_supply_pins, lvs_mismatches, fill_shapes, unannotated_nets, timing_corners, line or toggle, never checks (a search of src/nirmaan/company)
coverage over the design files is a separate tool (coverage.read), not part of the simulation verdict
